questions.prompt: A headless run has an approval service but no screen that can answer. A policy returns ask for a call. What happens?
options: The call runs, because nobody refused it
The harness waits until a person connects
The chain returns unavailable, and the call is denied with a reason saying no approval channel is available
The call is retried in the next step
questions.explanation: With no answerer, the approval/request chain reaches its end, which returns unavailable. The pipeline fails closed and denies the call.

questions.prompt: A person approves bash "git push". The model sends the same call again in the next step. What happens?
options: The harness asks again, because allowed-once covers one call
The call runs without asking, because the arguments match
The call is denied, because it was already run
questions.explanation: allowed-once is the only grant and it applies to one exact call. A new call needs a new answer.

questions.prompt: Why does the pipeline give a different deny reason for rejected and for unavailable?
options: Because the record can store only one kind of reason
So the model can tell a person's no apart from there being nobody to ask
Because unavailable calls are retried automatically
Because rejected calls are never written to the record
questions.explanation: A person's no means stop and explain; no channel means nobody could answer. Distinct reasons let the model act on the right one.
